study.title: Influence of Acupuncture Stimulation on Cerebral Network in Functional Diarrhea
study.study_design: Prospective pre-post fMRI study with two parallel groups (FD patients and healthy controls), both receiving active acupuncture
study.population: Eighteen FD patients and eighteen age- and sex-matched right-handed healthy controls
study.inclusion_criteria: (1) Patients were right-handed and aged between 20 and 30 years; (2) they matched the Rome III diagnosis criteria for FD; (3) they did not use gastrointestinal drugs for one week before enrollment in the study; (4) they were not participating in other clinical trials; and (5) they signed an informed-consent form
study.exclusion_criteria: (1) Patients had diarrhea caused by organic disorders; (2) they suffered psychosis or bleeding disorders; (3) they suffered serious disease of the heart, liver, kidneys, or other severe illnesses; (4) suffered from severe depressive or anxiety symptoms (the scores of the Self-rating Depression Scale (SDS) or Self-rating Anxiety Scale (SAS) were greater than 75); (5) they had a combination of severe headache or migraine relieved by bed rest or medicine or had a history of head trauma with loss of consciousness, (6) they had a combination of severe dysmenorrhea relieved by bed rest or medicine; (7) they were pregnant, preparing to be pregnant or lactating; or (8) had any contraindications to acupuncture or fMRI

extraction_notes.note: No coordinate tables were provided in the paper. All neuroimaging results (ReHo changes and functional connectivity changes) are presented in figures (Figure 2 and Figure 4) only, with region names described in text. No MNI or Talairach coordinates, cluster sizes, t-statistics, or z-statistics are reported for any brain region.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results Sections 3.3 and 3.4, Figures 2 and 4, Pages 4-6

extraction_notes.note: No sham acupuncture or placebo control arm was included. Both FD and HC groups received real acupuncture at ST25. This limits interpretation of specificity of acupuncture effects.
Expectancy, credibility, and blinding success were not assessed or reported in this study.
Adverse events were not reported anywhere in the paper.
Ethics approval committee name/number was not reported.
Trial registration number was not reported.

The paper states defecation frequency and BSFS were assessed 'throughout the second week' for outcome, but it is unclear whether baseline clinical measures were also measured over a week or at a single timepoint. The baseline appears to be a one-week pre-treatment period from Figure 1(b).

The exact type of correlation test used for the brain-behavior correlation (ReHo in left ACC vs defecation frequency change) was not specified (Pearson vs Spearman). The paper reports r = −0.6688 but does not name the test.
extraction_notes.source_location: Results Section 3.3, Figure 3(b), Methods Section 2.6, Page 3-5

extraction_notes.note: The coordinate space (MNI vs Talairach) is not explicitly stated in the paper. Normalization was performed to 'standard MNI template in SPM5', so MNI space is inferred, but no explicit statement about coordinate space for results is made.

Figure 2 shows colored ReHo change maps for FD and HC groups with slice numbers (45, 8, -1, -31, -1 for FD and 45, 8, -1, 4, -28 for HC) but no coordinates, cluster statistics, or tabulated peak data are provided. The axial slice numbers in figures cannot be treated as MNI z-coordinates.

Figure 4 shows colored functional connectivity network maps for FD and HC groups with slice numbers (8, 9, 14, -12 for FD and 8, 9, 14, 23 for HC) but no coordinates, cluster statistics, or tabulated edge data are provided.

Quantitative deqi measurement was not performed. The paper only states deqi sensations were intended (soreness, numbness, distention, and heaviness) and used as the endpoint of needle manipulation, but no formal deqi rating instrument (e.g., MASS, Southampton Needle Sensation Questionnaire) was applied.
The paper does not report whether informed consent included neuroimaging procedures separately, and no ethics committee reference number is provided.

Flip angle was reported as 90° for functional EPI sequences. Structural scan parameters list TR=1900ms, TE=2.26ms with 256x256mm² matrix, and data matrix 256x256. Functional EPI: TR=2000ms, TE=30ms, FOV 240x240mm², data matrix 64x64, 30 slices 5mm thick, 180 volumes. These are extracted as reported.

The left ACC was selected as the seed for functional connectivity analysis based on the ReHo-clinical symptom correlation result. This post-hoc seed selection based on the same dataset introduces circularity and should be noted for meta-analytic use.

The paper reports 'HS group' in Results Section 3.4 ('the precentral gyrus and inferior frontal gyrus of the HS group') which appears to be a typographic error for 'HC group' (healthy controls). This is preserved as reported in the source text.
